sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 09.12.2023 at about 6.45 p.m., the Petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HP-4948 from Madhugiri towards Dabaspet and when he reached near Koratagere- Tumkur Bypass road, Hulikunte Cross, Koratagere Town side, at that time, the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AB-5096 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) came from opposite direction i.e., Tumkur side in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained Type 3B Compound fracture left tibia+fibula and other injury all over the body.

He was immediately taken to Koratagere Govt. Hospital, after first aid, he was shifted to Tumkur District Hospital, wherein doctor advised for higher treatment, thereafter, petitioner was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and due to unavailability of bed at Victoria Hospital, he was shifted to Asian Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that the Petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.
Before the accident, Petitioner was hale and healthy, he was doing labourer work and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.

As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being insured and insurer of the offending vehicle .
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statements.

4. Respondent No.1 - Insurance company has filed its written statement and denied all the averments of the petition inter alia contending that the owner of the offending vehicle and the police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has admitted the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

It has denied that the accident has occurred due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that petitioner himself was solely responsible for the accident, as he was riding the motor cycle in a negligent manner, without wearing helmet and without having DL.
Further, it has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL.
It has denied the involvement of offending vehicle and it was falsely implicated.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.
On these grounds, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident occurred on 09.12.2023 at about 6.45 p.m., near Hulikunte Cross,

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case,
Dr. Vijayalakshmi S.H., Medical Officer, Taluk Govt. Hospital, Koratagere, Tumakuru District is examined as PW-2, one Nishith, Medical Record Incharge (Officer) at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Rajiv Gandhi Nagar, Nandhini Layout, Bengaluru is examined as PW-3 and Dr. Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center is examined as PW-4 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.21.

8. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 09.12.2023 at about 6.45 p.m., the Petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HP- 4948 from Madhugiri towards Dabaspet and when he reached near Koratagere-Tumkur Bypass road, Hulikunte Cross, Koratagere Town side, at that time, the driver of the offending vehicle came from opposite direction i.e., Tumkur side in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle.
As a result, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1.

PW-1 has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, complaint at Ex.P.2, spot Mahazar at Ex.P.3, spot sketch at Ex.P.4, Notice under Sec.133 of MV Act at Ex.P.5 reply to notice at Ex.P.6, IMV report at Ex.P.7, Wound Certificate at Ex.P.8 and Charge sheet at Ex.P.9, Discharge summary at Ex.P.10 and copy of Aadhaar card at Ex.P.11.

Further, Dr. Vijayalakshmi S.H., Medical Officer, Taluk Govt. Hospital, Koratagere,
Tumakuru District is examined as PW-2 and she has produced documents at Ex.P.12 to 16.

sentences.text: 12. The respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was a self accident.
The Ex.
P.1 to
Ex .P.8 i.e., police records establish that the accident occurred, due to negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
During the cross examination he has put forth the said suggestions, however, PW1 denied the same.
In the cross-examination of PW-1 nothing favorable to the respondent is extracted.
EX P17 MLC stated that " RT, at Holavanahalli cross, patient driving 2 wheeler, hit by -TATA ACE.
Thus , it becomes that it was not a self accident.

13. Except cross-examination and contention in the objections, respondent no 2-insurance company has not produced any evidence to prove that the accident has not occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was caused due to negligent act of the rider of the motorcycle.
14. By looking into the oral and documentary evidence it is clear that accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injury in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

15. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P.8 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Left leg, lower 1/3 open fracture,
2. Type III B Compound fracture tibia + fibula left leg,
3. ORIF EX fixation of left tibia and fibula injury Doctor opined that the said injury 1 is grievous in nature.
16. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Koratagere Govt. Hospital, after first aid, he was shifted to District Hospital, Tumakuru wherein doctor advised for higher treatment.

Thereafter, petitioner was shifted to Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru and due to unavailability of bed at Victoria Hospital, he was shifted to Asian Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was doing labour work and earning a sum of 30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.

He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
17.
The Petitioner has examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N., an Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental center, as Pw-4 and he has produced the 2 documents at Ex.P.20 and 21.

sentences.text: He was admitted to Govt. Hospital, Nelamangala for two months and got admitted to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital and underwent external fixator removal, left tibia CRIF with IMIL nail with wound debridement and SSG on 28.03.2024 and discharged on 31.03.2024.
PW-4 has examined the Petitioner clinically and radiologically while assessing the disability.
He found that Petitioner has unstable gait, walks with caution, deformed left leg, with severe wasting of the left calf muscles, restricted left knee and ankle movement.
He has assessed the total disability of the Left lower limb at 42% and whole body physical disability at 14%.
19. PW-4 in his cross-examination has stated that he has not treated the Petitioner.
He has stated that fracture is united with implants in situ.
He denied that he assessed the disability on the higher side.
It is pertinent to note that PW4 has assessed only physical disability and not the functional disability.
20. Considering the grievous injury and considering the difficulties, avocation and evidence of PW-4 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.
21. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 21 years.

Ex.P.11 - Aadhaar card of the petitioner shows that he was born on 06.02.2002, the same is considered, then age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 21 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.
22.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted in Kanva Sri Sai Hospital.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was doing labour work and was earning Rs.30,000/- P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.

In the absence of material with regard to source of income,
the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
23. The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,000/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
24. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:

Looking into the nature of injuries,
they would affect the working capacity of any person.

As the Petitioner is doing labourer work,
considering nature of injury and doctor's testimony, petitioner's the total functional disability is considered at 10%.

Thus, loss of future income comes to Rs.16,000 x 12 x 18 x 10/100=
Rs.3,45,600/- towards loss of future income.
25. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained grievous injury and was inpatient for a period of 13 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .50,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.

sentences.text: Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .30,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
27. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12 amounting to Rs.6,39,250/-.
On perusal of medical bills, it appears that the petitioner has spent Rs.6,39,250/- towards medical expenses.
They appear to be genuine.

Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of .6,39,250/-
towards Medical Expenses.
28. Future medical expenses:
PW-4 has stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which costs Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of material evidence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.

29. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges: Ex.P.10 -Discharge summaries shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Asian hospital from 10.12.2023 to 17.12.2023 i.e, for a period of 8 days and at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital from 27.03.2024 to 31.03.2024 i.e., for a period of 5 days totally for a period of 13 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .20,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
30. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 13 days admission in the hospital as inpatient and around three months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for three months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 3 = Rs.48,000/-.
31.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:

50,000/-

Medical expenses .

 6. Conveyance, Food, .
Nourishment & Attendant  charges

7. Loss of income during . 48,000/-
 laid up period

Total . 11,47,850/-
32. Liability:
Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However, Respondent Girisha Alias Girish vs Maruthi R on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143674035/
6 No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.

sentences.text: With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
33. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.11,47,850/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 2 years and balance 75% shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
